opportunities.title: D&D's 2027 Roadmap, Decoded: What 'Seasons' Actually Means for Your Table
opportunities.why_now: The new season-based roadmap (Champions, Survival, Sword & Sorcery, Rebellion) just dropped at Gen Con and readers need the structure explained in rules terms, not marketing terms.
opportunities.angle: Explainer breaking down what a 'season' is mechanically (book cadence, tie-in adventures, digital content) vs. past release models

opportunities.title: Dark Sun's Mature Rating Is a Rules Problem, Not Just a Marketing One
opportunities.why_now: Dark Sun was just announced as D&D's first mature-rated setting, raising immediate questions about how content ratings interact with the actual rules text (defiling magic, slavery mechanics, etc.).
opportunities.angle: Rules-first analysis of what a 'mature rating' could mean for published mechanics—is it just art/tone, or will subsystems (like defiling) get harsher rules treatment?

opportunities.title: Universes Beyond Meets 5e Rules: Can Star Wars and WoW Actually Fit the Chassis?
opportunities.why_now: D&D just announced Universes Beyond crossovers (Star Wars for Season of Rebellion, WoW this November) and the core question every rules-focused reader will ask is how these IPs get statted into 5e's system.
opportunities.angle: Rules-crunch speculation piece: what subclasses/mechanics would be needed to make lightsabers or WoW races work within existing 5e frameworks

opportunities.title: D&D's Third-Party Setting Partnerships: What 'Official Support' Actually Grants
opportunities.why_now: D&D just announced official third-party partnerships for popular campaign settings, and rules-minded readers want to know exactly what 'official' unlocks—stat blocks, rules legality, organized play?
opportunities.angle: Breakdown of what official third-party support historically has meant (5e compatibility license, playtesting, canon status) applied to this new announcement

opportunities.title: Vampire: The Masquerade's New Edition — What Rules Actually Change
opportunities.why_now: A new V:tM edition was just announced alongside more World of Darkness games, and the rules-first audience wants a clean comparison to prior editions before hype cycles take over.
opportunities.angle: Rules comparison piece anticipating likely mechanical shifts (Hunger dice, clan mechanics) based on prior edition history and publisher statements
